text:
alex: FYI — got a customer on support about a sudden billing spike after they enabled streaming + tool calls. Traces show multiple retries generating the same tool outputs, and our token accounting looks like it counted all attempts.

maria: ugh. do we have a single repro or logs? customer id? :eyes:

alex: linked their trace: `trace/0x9f3a` — snippet below. they enabled streaming, hit an upstream transient, the SDK retried, and we replayed the generation + tool call on the server. billing delta ~3x normal.

sam: can you paste the log lines? curious if we double-increment at the tool-invocation layer or only at the final token tally.

alex: here — scrubbed:

```
{"request_id":"r-12","attempt":1,"phase":"generation","tokens_consume":420,"tool_calls":1,"status":"aborted"}
{"request_id":"r-12","attempt":2,"phase":"generation","tokens_consume":415,"tool_calls":1,"status":"committed"}
{"request_id":"r-12","attempt":2,"phase":"tool","tool":"search","tool_tokens":120,"status":"committed"}
```

alex: billing shows charged_tokens = 955 (420+415+120) even though attempt 1 was aborted/stopped by caller.

maria: that matches the complaint. We probably aggregate tokens by request_id across attempts instead of by committed attempts only.

li: implementation detail: streamer pushes partial chunks as they generate. If the client disconnects or we abort attempt 1, some chunks still passed through to internal pipeline and got counted. Our current metric emits `tokens.generated` on generation completion and `tokens.sent` on chunk flush — looks like billing used the union naively.

sam: two separate problems: 1) retries replaying tool calls (idempotency) and 2) how we decide which tokens to include in billing when attempts abort/truncate.

jordan: from console/telemetry POV customers want a clear breakdown: input vs output vs tool tokens, and a per-attempt view for troubleshooting. Could we add a streamed `token_breakdown` event at finalization that lists lists? (e.g., `[{attempt:2, status:committed, output:415, tool:120}]`)

maria: billing rules debate: should we charge for compute we'd already spent even if attempt aborted? we spent GPU cycles for attempt 1. Legal/regulatory/billing fairness matter here.

billing-bot: Policy note: current contract language charges for generated tokens. We have no explicit "only last attempt" clause. Changing semantics will affect revenue recognition. Ping finance if we change retroactively.

alex: proposal: two values surfaced and used differently: 1) `compute_tokens` = tokens generated by the runtime across all attempts (used for internal cost accounting) 2) `billed_tokens` = tokens attributed for customer billing (default: committed attempt tokens + tool tokens deduplicated by idempotency). Show both in console.

li: implementation sketch:
- add `attempt_id` and `attempt_status` (committed/aborted/failed) to logs
- only add to `billed_tokens` when `attempt_status==committed` OR when client confirmed receipt (edge case for partial streaming)
- for tool calls: require `idempotency_key` at invocation layer; billing increments on first successful commit per idempotency_key

sam: question: how do we define "committed" for streaming when we stream partial content and then truncate due to context limit? If we truncate final attempt mid-stream, is that "committed"?

li: good point. propose: finalization happens when the model run reaches an explicit terminal event: `stop_token`, `eos`, explicit ``finish`` from runtime, or SDK-level `end_of_stream` ACK from client. If none happens (connection closed mid-stream) mark attempt_status=`aborted` and do not include in `billed_tokens` unless `compute_policy==charge-on-generate` (tenant-level flag).

jordan: UX: expose tenant-level toggle in Console -> Billing settings: "Charge for generated tokens (incl. aborted attempts)" vs "Charge only for delivered/committed tokens" with explanations. Default keep current behavior but make opt-in for new behavior. Also add an events timeline in request view showing attempts, statuses, token counts.

maria: action items for engineering + billing:
- [ ] sam/li: implement attempt_id + attempt_status in logs/metrics (telemetry schema)
- [ ] li: add idempotency_key enforcement for tool_call layer and dedup logic
- [ ] sam/jordan: Console changes — settings toggle + per-request timeline panel
- [ ] maria/billing-bot: update billing docs & finance notify on policy change

sam: implementation notes: metric names we should add: `redwood.request.attempts.total`, `redwood.request.attempt.tokens.generated`, `redwood.request.attempt.tokens.sent`, `redwood.request.tool.invocations.unique`. Keep them taggable by tenant_id, attempt_id, attempt_status.

alex: for rollout we should do a canary: flip the console toggle for a small set of internal tenants, collect diffs between `compute_tokens` and `billed_tokens` over 48h, and then expand. Need a migration plan for historical invoices?

maria: as long as we don't retroactively change billed amounts, finance is happy. New reporting only.

ops-bot: deploy started: refactor/telemetry-attempt-id -> staging (sha: c7a1f) :rocket:

li: small note: SDKs should add support for sending `idempotency_key` for tool calls; fallback to server-generated key if absent but warn in logs. We'll add SDK lint rule.

jordan: also add a small "why did I get charged X tokens" help link in the request detail that explains attempt vs tool token logic. keep copy simple.

alex: thanks everyone. I'll collect these into an RFC doc tonight and link in this thread. If anyone sees a regulatory landmine about charging for aborted compute, ping Maria directly. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — will loop in finance in the RFC.

sam: I'll pick up the telemetry schema PR tomorrow.

jordan: I'll start wireframes for the per-request timeline panel.

li: will prototype idempotency enforcement for tool calls in the runtime.

alex: perfect. closing the loop here.
